axes.model_access:
It calls no model itself; it is an interface implementation called by clients.
It uses IANA timezone names and supports automatic system-timezone detection.
axes.runtime:
A local **Python** process communicating over stdio.

It depends on the Python MCP SDK 1.x (requires mcp>=1.29.0,<2); SDK 2.0 renamed the APIs this server uses.

A 2026-08-30 fix addressed security and compatibility issues of container bind mounts under Docker / Podman / SELinux.

Running directly with uvx, no pre-install needed, is recommended.
axes.local_files: **No file-access capability whatsoever.** No file reads or writes involved.
axes.background: Not supported. A single time query is a synchronous operation, ending with the client process.
axes.tools:
It provides 2 tools: `get_current_time` (current time in a given timezone)
and `convert_time` (conversion between timezones).
Output is structured time data, ready for direct consumption.
axes.context: Stateless. Each call is independent; no history is kept.
axes.permissions:
**No substantive permission risk**: no file access, no network access, writes no state.
Its entire permission set is "being able to query the current time and convert timezones".
axes.fit:
Gives an Agent reliable time and timezone-conversion capability.
Suits scenarios where the model should not guess the time (scheduling, cross-timezone collaboration).

mcp.transport:
Supports stdio, **and offers container deployment (Docker / Podman)**.

The 2026-08-30 bind-mount security/compatibility fix (including SELinux) is the same commit (#2205) as for fetch and git.

The official README (full-text verification 2026-10-08) gives only local-process integration (uvx / pip / Docker);
there is no official launch method for a remote transport.
mcp.auth:
No separate authentication layer, but **this server accesses no external resources**;
whether auth exists makes no security difference.
mcp.scope:
**No file or network access; reads and writes no external resources.**
Together with sequential-thinking it is the lowest permission-risk class; safe in sensitive environments.

sections.变更记录说明:
**This object has no standalone changelog page**; change records are in the directory's commit history:

| Date | Content |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-30 | Fix container bind-mount security and compatibility (same commit #2205 as fetch and git) |
| 2026-08-18 | Document the Python MCP 1.x version requirement |

**Note**: SDK 2.0 renamed the APIs this server uses, and the official side pins `mcp>=1.29.0,<2`.
If your environment has SDK 2.x installed, this server may fail to start.
sections.工具清单:
| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_current_time` | `timezone` (IANA name) | current time in the given timezone |
| `convert_time` | `source_timezone` `time` (HH:MM) `target_timezone` | timezone conversion |

**It uses IANA timezone names** (e.g. `America/New_York`), not UTC offsets.
That is also where it beats "letting the model do timezone math" — IANA names carry daylight-saving rules.
sections.权限评价:
**The lowest permission-risk class among MCP servers**:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Read files | ❌ none |
| Write files | ❌ none |
| Network access | ❌ none |
| Persisted state | ❌ none |
| Delete capability | ❌ none |

Its entire permission set is "being able to ask the system what time it is". This class of server deserves calling out —
it shows the MCP ecosystem also has zero-risk tools.
sections.安装:
The official recommendation is running directly with `uvx`, no pre-install needed:
```bash
uvx mcp-server-time
```
`pip install mcp-server-time` is also supported.
